title: Gather the requirements
summary: A workbook for Stage 1 of the Core Build Starter Guide: the process to follow, the questions to ask at each step, worked examples, exercises and a template to fill in. Stage 1 has no code. Its output is a written document, and every later stage takes its input from that document.

title: Pick the stack
summary: Stage 2 turns the written Stage 1 requirements into one tool per layer and the API style, a reason for each, and a list of settings. Answer the questions in 2.2 to 2.7, and the decision record in 2.8 fills itself in as you go.

title: Settle the versions
summary: Stage 3 fixes which release of every tool the application is built on. It also writes two rules: how the application's own API may change, and how quickly updates reach live after launch.

title: Structure the backend
summary: Stage 4 ends with a repository that holds the lock files, a protected main branch with CI, the folder tree, the interfaces and a main.py index, and a design that an AI assistant has critiqued. This workbook breaks the stage into eight steps, 4.1 to 4.8. Each step has how to do it, the User Notices files it produces, an exercise, and how to check it. No function bodies are written in Stage 4; Stage 5 writes them from the interfaces.

title: Working in Git
summary: Companion to the Core Build Starter Guide , Working in Git. Read that chapter first; this workbook adds detail and does not change its rules.

title: Build the skeleton
summary: Stage 5 turns the Stage 4 interfaces into a backend that runs on your machine. You write every function's signature and comment, an AI assistant writes the bodies, you review each body against its comment and against the security checklist, you test it, and you trace one failure with the debugger. This workbook breaks the seven Stage 5 steps into smaller tasks, with diagrams, code you can copy, scenarios and practice exercises, all using the User Notices example.

files.label: The User Notices project at the end of Stage 5

title: Connect the front end
summary: Stage 6 connects each screen from Stage 1 to the backend functions from Stage 5, and makes sign-in work from end to end. When it is done, every screen is a page with a route, every page gets its data through an API call to /v1 , and a list records what each page sends and reads. Stage 7 designs the tables from that list.

title: Build the database
summary: Stage 7 replaces the Stage 5 stub with a PostgreSQL database designed from the fields the application uses. You list every field, group the fields into tables whose columns have types and constraints, add an audit table the application can add to but not change, add views and indexes, apply the schema through Alembic migrations that each have a tested downgrade, and connect the backend so the full request path runs against real tables.

title: Prepare for load
summary: Stage 8 decides which load layers the application needs, using measurements instead of guesses. This workbook breaks the stage into ten parts, with the commands, code and configuration a first-time builder needs, and labs you can run in this page.

title: Test and deploy
summary: Stage 9 takes the application that passed Stage 8 and puts it on two servers, a sandbox (a second copy of the deployment, used for testing) and live, with every test result recorded before the first user signs in.

title: Operate after launch
summary: Stage 10 sets up the routines that keep User Notices running, recoverable and current after launch: logs kept for their period, errors and alerts that reach a named person, a rollback written before it is needed, monthly restores, patching on a calendar, secret rotation and an incident log.
